incidents.cause: The flight instructor's lack of action to correct a high and fast landing approach which resulted in a long landing, and subsequent collision with a snow berm at the end of the runway. Contributing to the accident was the student pilot's improper approach.
The pilot's improper flare during a gusty, crosswind landing.
The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during the takeoff roll. Contributing to the accident was the pilot’s attempt to take off with full flaps.
The pilot’s decision to land the airplane in crosswind conditions that exceeded the airplane’s maximum demonstrated crosswind velocity.
The pilot's failure to maintain aircraft control due to spatial disorientation. Contributing to the accident was the night light conditions.
The pilot’s failure to maintain proper airspeed on approach in tailwind conditions, which resulted in an extended touchdown, bounced landing, and runway excursion.

The pilot's decision to depart under special VFR flight at night when instrument meteorological conditions prevailed at the departure airport and along the route of flight and his continued VFR flight into instrument meteorological conditions, which resulted in his spatial disorientation and subsequ
The student pilot’s non-stabilized approach and improper landing flare, which resulted in a hard landing.
Collision with a bird in flight, which resulted in damage to the right-wing leading-edge spar.

The noninstrument-rated pilot’s spatial disorientation and subsequent failure to maintain airplane control while operating over water in dark night conditions with reduced visibility due to rain in the area.
The pilot's failure to maintain directional control of the airplane while touching down during the landing.

The pilot's failure to maintain aircraft control during takeoff and his failure to ensure that the elevator trim was properly set before takeoff.  Contributing to the accident was the pilot's lack of autopilot system knowledge.
The student pilot’s failure to maintain a proper descent profile to avoid trees during the night visual approach and the flight instructor’s inadequate oversight.
The student pilot’s failure to maintain directional control during the landing roll with a crosswind.
The pilot's inadequate preflight inspection of the airplane and the subsequent total loss of engine power as a result of debris and water contamination in the fuel system.
The pilot's inadequate preflight weather planning and in-flight weather evaluation, which resulted in an encounter with a strong cold front and the pilot's subsequent loss of airplane control.

Incorrect installation of the oil temperature probe and an inadequate annual inspection that failed to detect leaking oil around the loose probe, which resulted in a catastrophic engine failure due to oil starvation.
A total loss of engine power during cruise flight due to fuel starvation as a result of a deteriorated fuel gasket.
A partial loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident examination did not reveal any anomalies that would have precluded normal operation.
A partial loss of engine power during the initial climb, which resulted in a forced, off-airport landing and impact with trees and a fence.

The failure of the left main landing gear upper side brace assembly during landing due to reverse bending fatigue as a result of the incomplete penetration of the circumferential weld during initial production of the component.
A loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined.
The pilot's failure to replace the oil filler cap following the preflight inspection, which resulted in a loss of engine oil and engine power, an emergency landing, and impact with terrain.
The pilot’s failure to attain the proper touchdown point during landing, which resulted in a runway overrun.
The pilot's failure to maintain clearance from another airplane in the formation flight due to sun glare.
The pilot's inadequate preflight planning and decision to take off at a high density altitude and in gusting wind conditions.

The flight instructor's exceedance of the critical angle of attack during a go-around, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall/spin. Contributing to the accident was the flight instructor's failure to familiarize himself with the flight characteristics of the unfamiliar airplane before conducting the

A total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation as a result of the pilot's inadequate fuel system management. Contributing to the accident were the pilot's diverted attention and failure to perform the prelanding checklist.

The pilot’s failure to maintain clearance between the longline and trees, which resulted in the longline snagging a tree and then recoiling into the main rotor blades and a subsequent loss of helicopter control.
The loss of engine power due to fuel starvation as a result of naphthenate fuel contamination, which blocked the fuel flow through the start pump.

The loss of power transmission to the main rotor for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident examination of the airframe and engine did not reveal any anomalies that would have precluded normal operation of the helicopter.
The pilot's failure to maintain control while landing in a high density altitude environment due to a loss of tail rotor effectiveness.

The pilot's decision to taxi the airplane from the roadway and his subsequent failure to maintain clearance from signs and a fence after a successful emergency landing following a total loss of engine power.
The pilot’s improper decision to land the airplane on a short runway with a tailwind and his subsequent delayed decision to abort the landing.
The pilot's selection of unsuitable terrain for landing the float-equipped airplane on a turf runway.
The pilot’s suicidal act.
An inadvertent collision with a deer during landing.
A loss of engine power during cruise flight for reasons that could not be determined because the engine was not properly preserved to prevent corrosion after the wreckage was recovered from the lake.

The total loss of engine power during climb after takeoff for reasons that could not be determined because postaccident examination did not reveal any anomalies that would have precluded normal operation.
A loss of engine power for reasons that could not be determined based on the available evidence.
A partial loss of engine power due to loose bolts holding the carburetor throttle body to the fuel bowl.
The pilot's failure to maintain directional control during landing in crosswind conditions, resulting in a loss of control and runway excursion.

A loss of engine power in cruise flight for reasons that could not be determined because a postaccident examination of the engine did not reveal any anomalies that would have precluded normal operation.
A loss of engine power during cruise flight for reasons that could not be determined.
The pilot's failure to adequately secure the airplane before hand-propping the engine for startup.
The pilot’s delayed use of carburetor heat, which resulted in carburetor icing and a subsequent total loss of engine power.
The pilot's mismanagement of the available fuel, which resulted in a total loss of engine power due to fuel starvation.
The pilot’s decision to maneuver the airplane at a low altitude, which resulted in impact with power lines and terrain.
A failure of the throttle control assembly for reasons that could not be determined based on available evidence, which resulted in a runway overrun and impact with an obstacle.

The left seated flight instructor’s improper manipulation of the landing gear position selection lever to the up position while still on the landing roll, which ultimately resulted in a landing gear collapse during a subsequent landing.
The pilot's exceedance of the airplane's critical angle of attack while maneuvering in the airport traffic pattern, which resulted in an aerodynamic stall and loss of control.
